name: Christ in the Old Testament
about: Types, shadows and prophecies fulfilled in Christ.

teachings.title: Thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter
teachings.summary: Zechariah 11 prophesies judgment on Judah's false shepherds and the breaking of the covenant, and his price of thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter is fulfilled in Judas' betrayal of the Good Shepherd.
teachings.text:
Continuing in Zechariah, we see the prophet turn from active encouragement in previous chapters to a more negative message and future prophecy against Judah.

The doors of Lebanon, the cedars, the oaks of Bashan, which is the fertile eastern bank of the Jordan, these represent the built temple, the great city Jerusalem, forged by the timber from these areas. Zechariah is prophesying their destruction, when reconstruction has hardly even begun.

The leaders, the shepherds, howl at their loss, the young lions roar, because the pride of Jordan is spoiled by false teachers and bad leadership at the judgment of God against them.

These wicked leaders, God says, slay the people and hold themselves not guilty. They sell them into servitude and think they are bless by the riches that comes to them for the price of men. The shepherds have no pity for their flock.

And God says this is His judgement on the Jews. Sort of the flip side of **Jeremiah 3:15**

*And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding*.

So, Zechariah preaches the destruction of the people at the hands of their neighbors and the kings and the Lord will not deliver them as He has so many times. As He just had from captivity. This is a future event.

God will feed the flock to the slaughter.

This all could be a prophecy of 70AD and the destruction of Jerusalem. The temple, as Christ said would come. Not on stone standing upon another. The scattering and spoil of the pride of the Jordan. The burning of the cedars and oaks. Or dual fulfilment with the days of vengeance, the end times prophecy of the destruction of Israel.

**Luke 21:21-22**
*Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto. For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.*

The prophet takes up two shepherd staves, and on one staff he writes "Beauty" and the other is called "Bands."

He says three shepherds he cut off in one month, and that he hated them and they hated him. False teachers, it seems. I can't say if this is Zechariah rebuking them, and taking their followers away from them, or God speaking directly that He did this to them. Either way, the flock of Judah is then cut off.

He breaks the staff "Beauty," which is the covenant with the people. Note the poor of the flock who believed on Him knew this was the word of the Lord. As a prophecy of Christ, and the new covenant that was established, the poor knew Jesus was the Word of the Lord.

Then he asks the people for his price as shepherd, and they set it at 30 pieces of silver. The parallel is obvious.

**Matthew 26:14-15**
*Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests, And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver*.

The good Shepherd, valued at only a lowly sum, 30 pieces of silver to be betrayed. And says to cast the sum to the potter.

**Matthew 27:3-7**
*Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that. And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself. And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in.*

The act of throwing the money to the potter was a symbolic rejection in Zechariah, and the purchase of the potter's field with the money is the fulfilment.

teachings.title: My God, why hast thou forsaken me
teachings.summary: Psalm 22 prophetically gives Christ's cry from the cross, when bearing the sin of all mankind as our scapegoat and High Priest He was forsaken by the Father that we might live.
teachings.text:
*Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?*

In the 9th hour, Jesus cried out from the cross the words of the Psalm, the opening line of a song of desperation, penned by David centuries earlier.

An event recorded twice in the gospels:

**Matthew 27:46**
*And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?*

**Mark 15:34**
*And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?*

The man Christ Jesus, after a day of betrayal, abuse, beaten beyond human recognition, scourged, shamed and mocked, cursed, hung on the tree, and become sin for all mankind, acknowledging in death that, by taking on all of the sin in all of creation, He is, in that moment, no longer looked upon by the Father Whom He has been with, and a part of, since everlasting.

The prophetic words of the Psalm, Christ's words echoed through time to the psalmist, words Jesus Himself knew from before the foundation of the world, conveying the heartbreaking moments before the perfect and holy Lord would willingly give His life that we may live.

Jesus cried out in Aramaic, the daily language of the people, the language He grew up in life speaking, conveying His humanity in that moment.

The Hebrew words, long sung by Israel in the congregation, translated, and again, interpreted into Greek, and given to us in English, never losing a scintilla of power. Given to us as the blessed hope, an example of the endurance and steadfastness we should look to:

**Hebrews 12:2-3**
*Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds*.

Jesus, our scapegoat, receiving our sin in atonement, without the camp. Taking them utterly away. Not as the blood of bulls and goats, offered yearly for sanctification by the High Priest of the Tabernacle, but once and for all, shed for man. And He, as THE High Priest, entered into the Heavenly Tabernacle, and applied His own precious blood upon the mercy seat in Heaven.

No greater love than this has ever been shed towards us, that God became flesh, and lived among us, sinless and perfect, that He might drink of this cup. Going to the cross that we might live.

The tragic nature of these words reveals the depth of the love of God. That while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

teachings.title: Psalm 22 and the sufferings of the cross
teachings.summary: Psalm 22 prophetically pictures the mockery, piercing, thirst and parted garments of Christ's crucifixion and the anguish He bore all His life, before turning to the hope that all things work together for good to them that love God.
teachings.text:
The prophetic nature of the God-inspired Psalm of David continues, showing the children of Israel the truth of Christ, through a glass darkly. In David's personal pain, we see a shadow of the suffering of Jesus, a reproach of men, despised of the people, laughed to scorn.

**Matthew 27:39–43**
*And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads, And saying, Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself. If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross. Likewise also the chief priests mocking him, with the scribes and elders, said, He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him. He trusted in God; let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of God.*

Compassed about by bulls, by dogs, men like lions, surrounded by the Roman soldiers doing the work of the Jews, piercing Jesus' hands and feet with nails. Splayed out upon the cross, His joints distended and twisted to support the weight of His body. The sinking feeling of death settling in His guts, as He struggled to breathe. His bones in sharp relief to His stretched out skin.

Crying out for water, Jesus is given vinegar to drink, raised up on hyssop, a bitter gall that could not quench His overwhelming thirst. The soldiers then parted His garments by lot:

**Matthew 27:34–35**
*They gave him vinegar to drink mingled with gall: and when he had tasted thereof, he would not drink. And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.*

The desperation and loneliness, the mental anguish Jesus suffered on the cross, He had also carried with Him for 33 years. Understanding the suffering that awaited Him at Calvary, knowing His anointed part in the great redemptive plan, while at all points being touched by the infirmity of the flesh, and tempted as we are. His prayers at Gethsemane, Son to the Father, that if it were possible to take this cup from Him, please let it be so. But steadfast to do the will of the Father, even knowing the physical and emotional pain He would endure. These stanzas in this psalm tragically capture it all, before transitioning to the joyful hope found in every tribulation those who love God can take comfort in:

**Romans 8:28**
*And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

teachings.title: Anointed with the oil of gladness
teachings.summary: The anointing of the king in Psalm 45 pictures Jesus anointed by the Spirit without measure, exalted after the cross, who gives believers the anointing of the Spirit by faith.
teachings.text:
After establishing His love for righteousness, the text states that He is anointed with the *oil of gladness* and that His garments smell of myrrh, aloes, and cassia.

As messianic prophecy, the elements of His anointment listed are symbols of Jesus, His death and His triumph over death.

The oil of gladness, olive oil, used to anoint kings and in celebration. To freshen the face, and to signify joy.

We see throughout scripture that oil is used as a metaphor for the Spirit. And Jesus, at the start of His ministry is anointed by the Spirit from the Father, showing to John and the other witnesses that Jesus was the Christ.

**Matthew 3:16-17**
*And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.*

While earthly kings were anointed with physical oil, Jesus was anointed directly by the Holy Spirit without measure.

**John 3:33–35**
*He that hath received his testimony hath set to his seal that God is true. For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for God giveth not the Spirit by measure unto him. The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.*

And so, the ultimate joy, the true anointing Is given to Jesus the Christ.

**Philippians 2:8–10**
*And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth*

The meekness of the sinless Son of God, going to the cross, despising the shame to be raised into glory, as the King of righteousness. The truth by which we are set free.

**Isaiah 61** says that He that was anointed by the Spirit of God to *preach good tidings to the meek..bind up the brokenhearted...proclaim liberty to the captives,* and to give unto them that trust in that truth..*.the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.*

The Messiah, the Anointed One, the Christ gives us the anointing of the Spirit by faith, that we may be His fruit, the trees of righteousness, planted that He might be glorified.

teachings.title: The tabernacle, a pattern of heavenly things
teachings.summary: Every part of the tabernacle is a picture of Christ and the Christian life: the freewill offering of accepting the gospel, the ark as the covenant written on our hearts, the shewbread as God's word, and the candlestick as the light of Christ.
teachings.text:
Transitioning from the previous chapters where the law of the covenant was given to the children of Israel and accepted in the blood of Moses sacrifices, God begins to instruct on the ceremonial ordinances, specific the building of the Tabernacle. The tent dwelling of God among His people.

It is important to understand that everything in this is a picture of Christ and the spiritual application is of Christianity.

**Hebrews 9**
*23 It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.*

*24 For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:*

The sanctuary, or holy place made with human hands represents the spiritual.

God says take the free will offering of the people to build with. They have to willingly offer to build the sanctuary. Our free will acceptance of the Gospel.

Then, God starts His instruction with the Arl of the Covenant, which will be kept in the heart of the Tabernacle. Where His angels protect His word, the stone tablets of the law, which are now written on our hearts.

**Hebrews 10:16**
*This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them*

And so here we see that this is where the covenant is kept; in our hearts, just as the Ark containing the old covenant was kept in the heart of the Tabernacle.

We see that it is the mercy seat, the seat of judgment of God, overseen by His angels, just as we as believers are.

**Hebrews 8:5**
*Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.*

Next God instructs that a table be made before the Ark, and on it the shewbread, bread left daily in the Tabernacle and temple. The daily bread, which is God's word.

**Deuteronomy 8:3**
*And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live.*

Then the candlestick, with the 7 candle holders, a picture of the light of Christ. The light of life. The 7 candles, the 7 spirits of God.

**John 8:12**
*Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.*

Jesus has the 7 spirits of God; the Spirit of the Lord, and the Spirits of wisdom, of understanding, of counsel, of might, of knowledge and of fear of the LORD.

And God says again; *And look that thou make them after their pattern, which was shewed thee in the mount.*

teachings.title: The camps of Israel and the throne of God
teachings.summary: The four standards of Israel's camps around the tabernacle mirror the four living creatures around God's throne in Ezekiel and Revelation, because the tabernacle was made after the pattern of the things in heaven.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 4:1-9**
*After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven: and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter. And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne. And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald. And round about the throne were four and twenty seats: and upon the seats I saw four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold. And out of the throne proceeded lightnings and thunderings and voices: and there were seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God. And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal: and in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, were four beasts full of eyes before and behind.*

*And the first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying eagle.*

*And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come. And when those beasts give glory and honour and thanks to him that sat on the throne, who liveth for ever and ever...*

**Ezekiel 1:3-10**
*The word of the Lord came expressly unto Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the Lord was there upon him. And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire.Also out of the midst thereof came the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance; they had the likeness of a man. And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings. And their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot: and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass. And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and they four had their faces and their wings. Their wings were joined one to another; they turned not when they went; they went every one straight forward.*

*As for the likeness of their faces, they four had the face of a man, and the face of a lion, on the right side: and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face of an eagle.*

**Ezekiel 10:14**
*And every one had four faces: the first face was the face of a cherub, and the second face was the face of a man, and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.*

**Numbers 2:1-2**
 *And the Lord spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying, Every man of the children of Israel shall pitch by his own standard, with the ensign of their father's house: far off about the tabernacle of the congregation shall they pitch.*

Each camp, Judah, Ruben, Ephraim and Dan had a banner. And each banner, and ensign; also called a symbol or crest.

The camps surrounding the Tabernacle containing the Ark of the Covenant, the throne of God. His mercy seat. The creation of which was a pattern shown Moses, reflecting the things in Heaven.

**Hebrews 8:1-5**
*Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens; A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man. For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer.*

teachings.title: Jerusalem, where God placed His name
teachings.summary: Jerusalem and Mount Moriah, where God chose to place His name and provided the ram for Isaac, point to Christ, the name God placed there to be sacrificed and to reign.
teachings.text:
Jerusalem, was chosen by God to "place His name";

**Deuteronomy 12:5, 11**
*But unto the place which the LORD your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there, even unto his habitation shall ye seek, and thither thou shalt come...Then there shall be a place which the LORD your God shall choose to cause his name to dwell there; thither shall ye bring all that I command you; your burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, your tithes, and the heave offering of your hand, and all your choice vows which ye vow unto the LORD*

The OT scriptures repeatedly say that Jerusalem is where God chose to place His name. Where the Son of God would be revealed. Where His name would be killed for our transgressions:

**Isaiah 53:3–5**
*He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not. Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.*

The same place Abraham was told to bring Isaac, at Mount Moriah, Zion:

**Genesis 22:2**
*And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.*

But God did not require the sacrifice of man, but rather gave His only begotten Son:

**Genesis 22:8**
*And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.*

In this place, where the altar was made, and the son was to be sacrificed, where a ram without blemish was caught in the thick of thorns was provided, Abraham recognized it for what it was:

**Genesis 22:14**
*And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovahjireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen.*

The place where the temple would be, pointing to the Messiah:

**1 Kings 8:28–29**
*Yet have thou respect unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O LORD my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer, which thy servant prayeth before thee to day: That thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day, even toward the place of which thou hast said, My name shall be there: that thou mayest hearken unto the prayer which thy servant shall make toward this place.*

God says that His promise to David that the anointed one would come from his line, and His determined use of Jerusalem as the city where He would place His name, is the only reason He did not wipe out Judah as He did Israel.

**Isaiah 37:34–35**
*By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.*

**Zechariah 9:9**
*Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.*

There, in Jerusalem would He place His name, Christ Jesus. The Alpha and Omega. The Lord of lords and King of kings.

**Isaiah 9:6**
*For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.*

teachings.title: Not a bone of Him broken
teachings.summary: Psalm 34's unbroken bones, fulfilled at the cross and pictured in the Passover lamb, show that all scripture points to Jesus and that God keeps His prophetic promises.
teachings.text:
In addition to the worship and praise of God, the recognition that His burden is light and He rewards us for bearing it, and the comfort that in our suffering and trouble, He is there, working it for good, **Psalm 34** contains a prophetic verse of Christ;

*He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.*

**John 19:31–37**
*The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away. Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him. But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs: But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water. And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might believe. For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken. And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.*

Nothing in Scripture is incidental, accidental or coincidental. And ultimately, everything points to Jesus.

**Exodus 12:46**
*In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.*

The Passover lamb being a clear type of Christ, the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. The instructions repeated again, to emphasize the importance:

**Numbers 9:12**
*They shall leave none of it unto the morning, nor break any bone of it: according to all the ordinances of the passover they shall keep it.*

The picture of Christ given throughout Old Testament scripture shows the power of His word, knowing the end from the beginning.

**1 Corinthians 1:27–29**
*But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence.*

There is no wisdom of this world that can explain the prophetic nature of scripture. It is foolishness to those that reject the truth. Yet the sheer overwhelming number of things which are not that become things that are, shows the glory of God and the folly of man.

 And the faithfulness of prophecy shows us the power of God to keep His promises, and increase our faith. Amen

teachings.title: The veil rent: come boldly to the throne
teachings.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
teachings.summary: The high priest entered behind the veil only once a year, but Christ's death rent the veil, so believers may come boldly before God at any time through Christ our high priest.
teachings.text:
Now to the narrative of events, following the deaths of Aaron's sons, God provided Aaron with an assurance that if he came before the presence of God, beyond the veil, under the ceremonial ordinances laid out; his sin offering, the linen robes and mitre that were holy, his washings, etc, that the Lord promises he will not be struck down as well. Remember, their sin was in adding to the ordinances their own doctrine, using strange fire and not the fire the Lord has provided.

And so the high priest would only enter the holy place, behind the veil, once a year to fulfill these sacrifices of atonement, first for himself and then all the people.

But when Christ had died, that veil was torn. As told by Matthew:

*And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent*...

And as Paul wrote of the veil and the unbelieving Jews:

2 Corinthians 3:14-18
*but their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ. But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart. Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away. Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.*

And so we know we may go before the Lord boldly, and at any time, because Christ is our high priest;

**Hebrews 4:14-16**
*Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession. For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.*

Because we have been made heirs, the sons of God and given access to the Lord by His grace and mercy, through faith in His Son;

**Ephesians 2:6**
*And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus*

For God is not slack concerning His promises.

**1 John 1:9**
 *If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.*

teachings.title: Why do the heathen rage
teachings.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
teachings.summary: Psalm 2 prophesies the rulers' vain rebellion against God's anointed, whom God raised up and set as King over the nations, warning rulers to kiss the Son and trust in Him.
teachings.text:
Why do the heathen rage? Why do people think they can go against God? Kings and rulers, presidents and prime ministers, popes and priests, all seek to be freed from the ways of the Lord, to do what they will.

Especially the religious and political leaders in the time of Jesus.

**Acts 4:27**
*For of a truth against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel, were gathered together*.

They believed if they killed the Son, they would break the bands, Their bonds, and be free of God.

Jesus addressed this in a parable, about a Lord who planted a vineyard and lent it out to husbandmen to dress and keep it. And when the Lord sent servants to gather the harvest, the stewards beat and killed them. So finally, the Lord sends his son;

**Matthew 21:38**
*But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance*.

David prophetically writes of this here in **Psalm 2**.

But, it is folly. The Lord holds them in derision. He laughs at their vain efforts, because Christ, His anointed, rose again.

He set His Son upon Zion, and upon the throne.

**Acts 13:32–33**
*And we declare unto you glad tidings, how that the promise which was made unto the fathers, God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.*

Jesus' inheritance are all the nations of the world, and possession of the uttermost parts of the world. And as Lord of lords and King of kings, He will rule them.

**Revelation 2:26–27**
*And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father.*

This prophetic Psalm gives warning to the rulers of this world, reminding them of their place. That they serve at the pleasure of the Lord, and He will deliver vengeance.

It's an amazing and consistent message, across the entire Bible; The Christ is God's anointed, and Jesus is the Christ. All who believe on Christ Jesus shall be saved. His grace and mercy giving us the chance to serve Him in righteousness.

*Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling. Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish from the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all they that put their trust in him.*

Amen

teachings.title: Myrrh, aloes and cassia on the King
teachings.theme: Christ our King and High Priest
teachings.summary: The spices on the King's garments in Psalm 45 picture the gospel: myrrh His sacrificial death, aloes His incorruption and resurrection, and cassia His ascension and eternal priesthood.
teachings.text:
The anointing oil is based on olive oil, but contains the other spices for fragrance, myrrh and cassia.

**Exodus 30:22–29**
*Moreover the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, Take thou also unto thee principal spices, of pure myrrh five hundred shekels, and of sweet cinnamon half so much, even two hundred and fifty shekels, and of sweet calamus two hundred and fifty shekels, And of cassia five hundred shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, and of oil olive an hin: And thou shalt make it an oil of holy ointment, an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary: it shall be an holy anointing oil. And thou shalt anoint the tabernacle of the congregation therewith, and the ark of the testimony, And the table and all his vessels, and the candlestick and his vessels, and the altar of incense, And the altar of burnt offering with all his vessels, and the laver and his foot. And thou shalt sanctify them, that they may be most holy: whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy.*

This ointment is given of God to sanctify, and make all that it is applied to, holy. But it was reserved for the items of the Tabernacle and the High Priest, a holy anointing oil.

**Exodus 30:32**
*Upon man’s flesh shall it not be poured, neither shall ye make any other like it, after the composition of it: it is holy, and it shall be holy unto you.*

God also instructed not to anoint a stranger with this, as it is holy, threatening to cut off any who do it from the people.

Yet it is this holy oil, reserved for the things of God and His High Priest, that is given to the King described in **Psalm 45**.

Myrrh is a bitter resin extracted from a thorny tree, that was primarily used in burial preparations. It was given as a gift for a King by the wisemen visiting the infant Jesus.

Nicodemus used myrrh and aloes in the preparation of the body of Christ at His burial.

**John 19:39–40**
*And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight. Then took they the body of Jesus, and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury.*

There is a sense of the suffering of Christ, the death He tasted for all men, in the application of myrrh in the Psalm, reflected in the Gospels.

The scent of myrrh on the King carries with it His majesty, that cannot be separated from His sacrificial death. His garments carry the scent of His ultimate act of love.

The aloes mentioned are not the oil we know today, but the fragrance made from an eaglewood tree, and those aloes are found in Nicodemus' mixture. Because aloes were used to preserve bodies and counteract the smell of decay, they symbolize resurrection, healing, and incorruptibility of Christ, in His death.

**Psalms 16:10**
*For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.*

Cassia is an aromatic bark, like cinnamon, and is used in the holy anointing oil, mentioned above. This ties in to the understanding of Christ not only as King but High Priest.

Taken together, these three spices combined on the garments of the King paint a complete picture of the Gospel narrative. Myrrh as the sacrificial death, aloes His incorruption and resurrection, and cassia, Jesus' ascension, and role as High Priest, forever.

And so in **Psalm 45**, as the King approaches His bride, He carries with Him the literal aroma of redemption. The scent of His gospel. Amen

teachings.title: Psalm 45 and the conquering King
teachings.summary: Psalm 45, inspired by the Holy Ghost, prophesies Christ the bridegroom King whose truth, meekness and righteousness are the qualities believers should pursue.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 45** is a doctrine-rich wedding song, that speaks clearly of the Lord Jesus, a bride brought to Him, and the promise of exaltation for the King of Kings.

Of course, the dual nature is both a historic royal wedding song and a profound Messianic prophecy, the Psalms often capture both layers in a way that makes them relevant to our lives as believers. It is a testimony to their divine inspiration.

The same inspiration described in the introduction found in verse 1.

The author says his heart is inditing a good matter, meaning fit to burst with the understanding he is speaking of. His *tongue is the pen of a ready writer.*

God has given him the idea, the words, His inspired, God breathed need to speak and record the word of God, that is bubbling our of his heart.

Jesus said *out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh*, be it the evil of the Pharisees or the inspired word. Whether the penman, or those who have committed the word to our hearts.

**2 Peter 1:21**
*For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.*

And so, moved by the Holy Ghost, given the word of God, the ready writer gives us a song of romance and prophecy. Deeply layered and rich, as only scripture can be.

A similar song to Solomon's, messianic prophecy couched in a romantic allusion.

Verse 2 begins the description of One, fairer than all men, full of grace, blessed forever by God. The Christ. His chosen. The groom, and King.

Girded with His sword, the most mighty. Almighty. A name of God given this person. All glory and majesty are His.

Riding majestically, and prosperously, upon a horse to battle.

**Revelation 19:11-13**
*And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself. And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God*.

He has the word of God proceeding from His lips. Destroying the enemies of God with His sharp sword. The strength of His right hand, teaching *thee terrible things*.

What a picture that's painted. What a powerful, Almighty Son of God. Who comes to smite the enemies of His Father, and rule with a rod of iron, but His prosperity is in His truth and meekness and righteousness.

The terrible things, are in this context, the fearful lessons of the Lord. And these are grounded in those three qualities. The truth of the word, the meekness of our Savior, His righteousness in all things.

For the Christian, these three qualities are what we should pursue. We should gird ourselves with the sword of Truth, knowing His word in our hearts, ready to deliver it.

**Hebrews 4:12**
*For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

Living in meekness, a servant. Condescending to men of low estate, that they may be saved. Putting our heart to The afflicted, the widow, the fatherless, the poor. For the meek shall inherit the Earth.

And living in righteousness. Doing right things by the judgment of God found in His word. Cleansed by the blood and carrying the righteousness of Christ within us. Being holy, as He is holy.

*Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.*

Truth, meekness and righteousness means loving what is good and hating wickedness. This is the inheritance of the Lord and the perfection of it found in Christ Jesus.

**Hebrews 1:8–9**
*But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom. Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.*

teachings.title: Forget thy father's house: the bride of the King
teachings.summary: Psalm 45 pictures believers as the bride of Christ, called to love Him above family and nation as a wife leaves her parents, and to look not to earthly lineage but to the spiritual children they win to the gospel.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 45**, the messianic wedding song, we transition from the King to the bride.

At His right hand stands the queen, decked in gold from Ophir, (a site somewhere south-southwest of Jerusalem renown for its gold).

Her ornamental beauty, provided by the King, to set apart the bride. The honorable women, the church.

As a picture of believers, we see the Kings great desire for the beauty He has bestowed. He is truly Lord and we worship Him.

*Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house*

We are called to hear the appeal from Heaven, to consider and incline our ear (*faith cometh by hearing*), to forget our people and our parents, and to become His.

**Luke 14:26–27**
*If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.*

We are called out, to be His above our family or national bonds. To "hate" here doesn't mean to dislike intensely, as it does today. It means to not love as much, to not prefer over another. To love Christ more than even your kin.

**Matthew 10:35–37**
*For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household. He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.*

Just as a wife is called to separate from her parents and cleave unto the husband.

**Genesis 2:24**
*Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.*

Becoming the bride of Christ, cleaving unto Him, placing our love for Him above others. A wedding is a picture of this relationship that we have. It is given as a parable, that we may better know Him.

In our status as His, the great of every nation shall show us favor. Perhaps in the Millennial Kingdom, certainly not in this life. But when we have come into the inheritance, they will respect our rule because Jesus is their Lord, and we are His.

We are arrayed as a burden in gold and fine embroidery, the white garments of purity, the righteousness of Christ that covers us.

*With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought: they shall enter into the king’s palace*

**Luke 15:10**
*Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.*

This is the celebration of salvation. And the future wedding supper we are called to.

*Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, whom thou mayest make princes in all the earth.*

We will not look to our earthly heritage, the genealogies and lineage, but instead at those we have won to the Gospel, as children who rule and reign with Christ. It is our godly heritage, the spiritual children we present to Christ.

Looking forward to the future of those we have helped come to repentance. This is our vow to our Lord and Savior.

*I will make thy name to be remembered in all generations: therefore shall the people praise thee for ever and ever*. Amen

teachings.title: Rahab and the scarlet thread
teachings.summary: Rahab the harlot was saved by her faith in God and placed in the line of Christ, her scarlet thread a picture of His blood, showing God can redeem anyone who holds the faith.
teachings.text:
And so we are here in **Joshua** chapter 2, and the newly anointed leader of the Hebrews is about to lead the people over the Jordan and into the promised land.

His first act is to send 2 spies to spy out the walled city of Jericho. This is similar to an earlier appearance of Joshua, in **Numbers 13**, where Moses sent 12 spies into the land, and 10 spies were bad and 2 were good.

Joshua and Caleb were the good men, who had faith in God to deliver the land to them. The 10 cast doubt and fear.

Not wishing a repeat, apparently, Joshua sends only 2, and these men make their way into Jericho by way of the home of the harlot, Rahab. There she lodges them and hides the spies when the king of Jericho sends out men to find them. The harlot hides the men upon her roof and sends the kings men on a fruitless search back towards Jordan.

She tells the Hebrew spies that she has done this because the whole land knows that the Lord God is with them, and are friegtened of them, considering the miracles of the Red Sea and the defeat of the other Canaanite kings. She has faith that the same Lord God will bring them victory in Jericho. The spies thank her, and she asks that they swear her family will be protected in their eventual siege of the city. The spies grant her an oath. That if she places the scarlet thread she had let them down on in her window, that all within her household will be saved.

Her faith in God to deliver the Israelites, and her faith in the promise of the spies, will lead to her salvation, as we will see in a few chapters. And the same faith serves as a picture of Christ. The scarlet thread, like the blood on the door frames on the first Passover. The same scarlet thread of the blood of Christ that runs throughout the Bible.

And Rahab is part of that bloodline of Christ Jesus, as we see during the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew;

**Matthew 1:5-6**
*And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse; And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias*

The Greek spelling of 'Rachab,' is Rahab. She birthed Boaz of Judah, who eventually begets David, in the human lineage of Christ. A scarlet thread.

And she is saved by her faith, we know. Despite being a harlot. Despite her sinful life. She is redeemed, and honored with a mention in the Hall of Faith found in **Hebrews 11**, in the company of great Old Testament believers;

**Hebrews 11:31**
*By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace*.

She is also used by James, alongside Abraham, in his examples of those whose actions demonstrated to others the faith she had in her heart;

**James 2:25**
*Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?*

Given as an example of faith by God, to show us that He may use anyone for His purpose, and redeem anyone who holds the faith.

teachings.title: I am my beloved's
teachings.summary: The bride's choice to rise early and go forth with her beloved pictures the mature believer deliberately making Christ the centre of each day and working with Him to bear fruit in new believers.
teachings.text:
Song of Solomon 7 opens with the King, having called his beloved Shulamite woman to return to him that he may look upon her at the end of chapter 6, now detailing what he sees of his beloved. He describes her beauty and the perfect symmetry of her body.

*How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!*

Everything he sees of her is good. Just as we are seen as perfect and without spot when God looks upon us, clothed in the righteousness of Christ.

**2 Corinthians 11:2**
*For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.*

**Colossians 1:22**
*In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight*

**Jude 1:24–25**
*Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.*

The woman responds to her husband, her brother, her spouse with unwavering confidence;

*I am my beloved’s, and his desire is toward me.*

We are Christ's, and His desire is for us.

Beginning there in verse 10, she responds to her beloved, knowing she is his, and inviting him to go forth with her, to live with her. To get up early to the vineyards, to see the vine flourish and come to fruition, where she will give him her love.

The spiritual application here; She has gone from her initial humble acceptance of his love, to the joy of the wedding feast, to her period of complacency, persecution, profession of faith and renewal, to now making the decision to plan her day and life around him, is a beautiful picture of the Christian life.

A believer makes the conscious decision to make Jesus their companion. To go forth with Him and to reside with Him. To wake early in the morning, starting the day with Christ, and His word. In prayer.

This intentionality is contrasted with the bride laying in bed, hesitant to wake, making excuses to avoid letting in her beloved. As mature Christians, in it for the long haul, we seek Him first.

We work with Him to tend the vine, which is His church, bringing forth fruit which are new believers. Planting the seed of His word. Watering and nurturing. Tending to them, the babes in Christ, and helping them grow to maturity. Through it all, giving Him all our love.

We lay up our fruit, those people we have given the gospel to, the needy to whom we give comfort. The broken hearted we have consoled. This treasure we have laid up for Heaven, but to Him is the increase. We give Him our all because He is our beloved.

teachings.title: Jesus is the excellent name of the Lord
teachings.summary: Psalm 8 praises Christ, who is God, the Creator through whom all things were made, the I AM given the name above every name, and the only name under heaven by which men must be saved and worshipped.
teachings.text:
The excellent name of our Lord is Jesus.

**Psalm 8** is a song of praise for the Christ. The name of the Lord, who has been set by the LORD, God the Father, over all things. Who also is God.

Jesus is the anointed, Who is ordained to strength, and mighty.

**Hebrews 2:4–9**
*God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will? For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak. But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him? Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him. But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.*

The New Testament reveals the intent and interpretation of the Old. We see Jesus using Psalm 8:2 against the Pharisees, showing that He is the name of God;

**Matthew 21:15–17**
*And when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the son of David; they were sore displeased, And said unto him, Hearest thou what these say? And Jesus saith unto them, Yea; have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise? And he left them, and went out of the city into Bethany; and he lodged there*.

Through His name was all creation made:

**Colossians 1:16–17**
*For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.*

**John 1:1–3**
*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.*

*The same was in the beginning*, when men first called upon the name of the Lord.

**Genesis 4:25–26**
*And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.*

Jesus has been made to have dominion over all things, that the glory and honor be given to Him.

**Ephesians 1:9–10**
*Having made known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he hath purposed in himself: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him*

And the excellency of His name is revealed in Christ Jesus.

**Philippians 2:9–11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.*

Jesus is the name of the Lord. Of the great I Am.

**John 8:56–58**
*Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad. Then said the Jews unto him, Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham? Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.*

No other name is given by God to be worshipped as God.

**Acts 4:12**
*Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.*

teachings.title: Christ the King of all the earth
teachings.summary: Psalm 47 prophesies Jesus, who is God, ascending with a shout and returning with a trumpet to catch up the saints, reign as King of kings over every nation, and finally deliver the kingdom to the Father.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 47** is a song of praise for the Lord, the King of kings. Christ Jesus, Who shall put every nation under His feet.

**Revelation 11:15–17**
*And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever. And the four and twenty elders, which sat before God on their seats, fell upon their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, We give thee thanks, O LORD God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.*

He shall rule and reign with a rod of iron, and give to all His people their inheritance in His Kingdom.

Jesus is God. Verse 5 says *God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.* A prophetic Old Testament verse, made clear in the New Testament, carrying the comfort of all believers;

**1 Thessalonians 4:16–17**
*For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.*

We shall sing of the glories of the Lord, forever.

**Revelation 7:10–12**
*And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb. And all the angels stood round about the throne, and about the elders and the four beasts, and fell before the throne on their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, Amen: Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever. Amen.*

**Revelation 19:16**
*And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.*

For Jesus is the King of all the earth, and reigns over the heathen. All the nations. He is greatly exalted above every name.

**Philippians 2:9–11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.*

Jesus will reign over all things, and, having defeated death and been made ruler of all, He will give all to God the Father. A perfect sacrifice, holy and acceptable, made holy by His righteousness:

**1 Corinthians 15:24–27**
*Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power. For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death. For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him*.

**Psalm 47** is a wonderful and prophetic song of praise and worship for the Kingdom of God, under our Lord Christ Jesus. All honor and praise is His. Amen

teachings.title: Mount Zion, chosen of God
teachings.summary: Zion is holy because God placed His name there and separated it for His purposes, the place of Christ's sacrifice and future reign, not because its people are holy.
teachings.text:
Mount Zion, Jerusalem, is often referenced and praised as the place God chose to place His name. His holy city, the mountain providing natural protection on 3 sides, situated perfectly. A river running through the fertile valley. The setting where Abraham brought Issac. Where God prepared Himself a sacrifice. Where Jesus was slain and rose again, and where He will reign in the Kingdom to come.

The name, Zion, means a “monument; raised up; sepulcher,” the place of the tomb, hewn out of rock, the site of Christ's burial. Chosen by God.

Jerusalem, the city isn't a lonely peak, but rather a settlement nestled within a protective bowl of higher terrain, with Mt Moriah and the mount of Olives part of the limestone rings, defending the area.

**Psalm 125:1–2**
*They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever. As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the LORD is round about his people from henceforth even for ever.*

Beautiful for situation, a perfect location, the city if the great King on its north face.

**Psalm 132:13–14**
*For the LORD hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation. This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it.*

**1 Peter 2:5–6**
*Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.*

The shelter of Zion, the cornerstone of which is Christ, is where Jesus returns to in the end times, with the 144,000 witnesses.

**Revelation 14:1**
*And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads.*

The defenses of this holy mountain were enough to dissuade kings and armies.

Sennacherib, of Assyria, the most powerful emperor of the ancient world, invaded Judah with a massive army of 185,000 soldiers.

He sent his top military commanders to the walls of Jerusalem, fiercely mocking King Hezekiah and blaspheming God, confidently expecting the city to fall just like every other nation before it.

Hezekiah called out to the Lord for protection of the city.

**2 Kings 19:16–19**
*LORD, bow down thine ear, and hear: open, LORD, thine eyes, and see: and hear the words of Sennacherib, which hath sent him to reproach the living God. Of a truth, LORD, the kings of Assyria have destroyed the nations and their lands, And have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them. Now therefore, O LORD our God, I beseech thee, save thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art the LORD God, even thou only.*

And God harkened to the prayer, for His own purposes and will;

**2 Kings 19:32–34**
*Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a bank against it. By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.*

Zion is defended for His own sake, because He placed His name there, and for the promise made to David that out of Zion shall come a King.

**Romans 11:26–27**
*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Zion is holy, because it has been separated unto the purposes of God.

It is not holy because the people there are holy. God allowed Babylon to raze the city and remove the people. Jesus decreed that Jerusalem would fall, and in 70AD it did. With the end times approaching, the city is considered wicked;

teachings.title: Dark sayings made plain in Christ
teachings.summary: Parables and dark sayings filter the humble from the spiritually blind, but Christ opened all the Old Testament to show it points to Him, and the Spirit now reveals its meaning to believers.
teachings.text:
The call by David to hear and understand his "dark sayings and parables," brings to mind the way Jesus taught in His ministry.

**Matthew 13:34–35**
*All these things spake Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world*.

Jesus revealed to His disciples that parables act as a spiritual filter. To the humble seeker of wisdom, they provide deeper understanding; to the spiritually blind, they remain obscure "dark sayings."

**Matthew 13:10–13**
*And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables? He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given. For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath. Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand*.

The unfolding revelation to man throughout scripture was never meant to keep wisdom hidden. Especially, not forever.

Unlike the religions of man, with their esoteric knowledge, vague and shallow sayings fed in dribs and drabs, with no clarity ever given, God's word opens itself up, and Jesus ultimately shows what all these "dark sayings" and prophetic parables actually mean.

 **John 16:25**
*These things have I spoken unto you in proverbs: but the time cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in proverbs, but I shall shew you plainly of the Father.*

During His earthly ministry, even Jesus' most faithful disciples required His explanation of the parables He spoke in, to the crowds and Pharisees.

**Mark 4:33–34**
*And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it. But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.*

But the full revelation of scripture came in the days following His resurrection, when all things were finally made known.

To the men He met on the way, in **Luke 24**, Jesus, *beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself*.

And to the gathering of the disciples, He did the same;

**Luke 24:44–45**
*And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me. Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures*.

He explicitly references the three divisions of the Old Testament, (the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms, like Psalm 49) and grants them the spiritually supernatural ability to finally see past the "dark sayings" to understand the plain truth of the Gospel.

These things are revealed to us by the Spirit, Who teaches us all things. We are able to see the entire picture, fully revealed in Christ, and the understanding imparted by the Apostles in the Epistles for added clarity and depth. Only the future Revelation of Christ Jesus is still through a glass darkly, (although the gist is pretty clear on timing and events).

We see that the Old Testament scriptures aren't an empty recitation of genealogy, geography and events. They aren't the vain contemplations of man. They are the words of eternal life, and all these were written to point the way to Jesus, and provide us with understanding.

**1 Corinthians 10:11**
*Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.*

Not only does God's word exist to show us His ways, but ultimately it is the tool He has given us to fulfill the Great Commission, leading others to the truth.

teachings.title: The blood of the covenant and thanksgiving
teachings.summary: The Old Covenant sacrifices sealed in blood pictured Christ's once-for-all sacrifice, and God never needed them but desires thanksgiving, mercy and right judgment.
teachings.text:
The covenant was made by sacrifice; the blood of the covenant made by Moses and the people with God was sealed with blood that represented the blood of Christ, and the promise of a better covenant with God by sacrifice, the sacrifice of the Son.

**Hebrews 9:19–23**
*For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission. It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.*

The heavens declare the righteousness of Christ Jesus, and His righteousness is upon all His people. God is the judge Himself. The Atonement, Himself. The mediator, Himself.

The saints are secure in His righteousness. But God speaks to Israel in judgment. Beginning with His people.

*Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee: I am God, even thy God.*

The future prophecy versus the current call.

The continuous sacrifices made before God to give the physical nation of Israel the honor of being His people, keep His hand from reproving them harshly. They maintained the Levitical ordinances which He based promises on. The sacrifices that needed to be done constantly to maintain ritual cleanliness and keep His presence among them had been done. He isn't asking for more sacrifice. No additional bulls or goats to shed their blood.

Again, we have a better sacrifice, once and for all, a covenant made by the blood of Jesus, the burnt offering for our sin.

**Hebrews 9:11–14**
*But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?*

But, in the old covenant, the blood of bulls and goats were used, continually, signifying the Sacrifice to come, and this the Levites did.

God is telling His people at this time He isn't asking for more, and in fact it is not the blood of bulls and goats, and their burnt offering that He seeks.

Every beast is His. The cattle upon a thousand hills. If He were hungry, and in need of the savour of the fat and the sustenance of meats, He has His pick and fill. He doesn't need them. Their sacrifices are a picture and a necessity for the covenant, but they do not please Him in and of themselves.

**Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

Sentiment repeated by Christ;

**Matthew 12:7**
*But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.*

Here, in **Psalm 50**, God makes it clear that the offering is thanksgiving. They are vows to be paid to maintain their part in the covenant as His nation. Tithes and first fruits as acts of faith.

It is not, as other gods, a meal for Him to consume, but a thanksgiving offered to show gratitude for all that He has supplied them, and to keep themselves unspotted, and be His people.

God desires mercy towards others. Right judgment, defending the weak and hating the workers of iniquity.
